wagassi.title: Wagassi
wagassi.intro: Soft, fresh and gently salted, wagassi is the cheese of Fulani pastoral life—and an edible path into the landscapes of northern Benin.
wagassi.heading: A landscape,
wagassi.p1: Wagassi begins with fresh milk and the leaves of the calotropis plant, whose sap gently separates curds from whey. The method travels through families—measured less by recipe than by touch, sound and attention.
wagassi.p2: In markets across Benin you will see ivory rounds stacked neatly, sometimes stained rust-red with sorghum leaves. Grilled over charcoal or simmered in sauce, it becomes a bridge between pastoral north and coastal table.

amiwo.title: Amiwo
amiwo.intro: Red rice cooked with tomato, oil and often fish—a plate of belonging that anchors many southern tables.
amiwo.heading: Red of the coast,
amiwo.p1: Amiwo is less a single recipe than a family of gestures: rice absorbing tomato, oil, and the day’s catch. It shows up at celebrations and ordinary lunches alike.
amiwo.p2: Follow it from market stalls to home kitchens and you understand how a simple plate can carry region, memory and hospitality at once.

buy-local.title: Buy local · Cook together
buy-local.intro: The market is the beginning: choose what is fresh, learn the ingredients, cook without rushing.
buy-local.heading: Cook. Sit down.
buy-local.p1: Buying with someone who knows the stalls changes what you take home—and how you taste it later.
buy-local.p2: This is food as practice: attention, conversation, and a meal that does not need a restaurant to matter.

akassa.title: Akassa
akassa.intro: Fermented corn dough—soft, slightly tangy—the everyday companion to sauces, fish and conversation.
akassa.tryIt: With fish sauce or peanut sauce
akassa.heading: The dough that holds
akassa.p1: Akassa is less a dish than a structure: it receives sauce, fish, and the heat of the day without demanding attention.
akassa.p2: Find it by the water, in market stalls, and at family tables—always nearby when the real meal is the company.

grilled-fish.title: Grilled fish
grilled-fish.intro: Morning catch, charcoal, pili-pili—the coastal plate that needs almost nothing else.
grilled-fish.tryIt: At a street grill after dark
grilled-fish.heading: Fire, fish,
grilled-fish.p1: Along the coast the best meals are often the simplest: fish scored and grilled, a pile of attiéké or fried yam, a cold drink.
grilled-fish.p2: Follow the smoke after sunset and you are already inside the city's night rhythm.

pate.title: Pâte & sauce
pate.intro: The national pair: a smooth starch (cassava, corn or yam) with a sauce that carries the day.
pate.madeFrom: Cassava, corn or yam · local sauces
pate.tryIt: With a home cook if you can
pate.heading: One dough,
pate.p1: Pâte is the quiet constant. What changes is the sauce—tomato, peanut, leaf greens, fish—and who is stirring it.
pate.p2: Learning to eat it without hurry is part of learning the country.

dantokpa-bites.title: Dantokpa bites
dantokpa-bites.intro: A tasting path through one of West Africa's largest markets—fritters, fruit, grilled corners, and the people who feed the city.
dantokpa-bites.tryIt: With a local who knows the aisles
dantokpa-bites.heading: The market is
dantokpa-bites.p1: Dantokpa is not only where the city shops—it is where it eats on its feet between errands.
dantokpa-bites.p2: Go early, stay curious, and let someone who works there set the order of stops.

sodabi.title: Sodabi
sodabi.intro: Local palm spirit—approach with respect, share slowly, and listen to the stories that come with the bottle.
sodabi.tryIt: With hosts who offer it, not as a stunt
sodabi.heading: A spirit,
sodabi.p1: Sodabi is less a drink to conquer than a social signal—offered, accepted, and paced by the table.
sodabi.p2: Decline politely if you prefer; accept if you are ready to stay a while.

kpélé.title: Kpélé
kpélé.intro: Corn fritters from the street—crisp, hot, and gone in a few bites between errands.
kpélé.heading: Street heat,
kpélé.p1: Kpélé is the snack of motion: bought standing, eaten walking, remembered later.
kpélé.p2: It is not a restaurant dish. It is the city feeding itself between stops.

ablo.title: Ablo
ablo.intro: Steamed rice cakes—soft, mild, and often sold still warm from the steamer at the edge of the market.
ablo.heading: Steam,
ablo.p1: Ablo is quiet food: white, soft, and precise. It shows up at breakfast and between errands, less celebrated than red rice, just as present.
ablo.p2: Buy it where the steamer is still working. Heat and timing matter more than any written recipe.

atassi.title: Atassi
atassi.intro: Rice and beans cooked together—everyday fuel that holds workers, students and long afternoons.
atassi.tryIt: With fried egg or fish when available
atassi.heading: The plate that keeps the day going.
atassi.p1: Atassi is not festival food. It is the reliable middle of the day—filling, affordable, and shaped by whoever is cooking that street corner.
atassi.p2: Follow the queues more than the signs. The best versions rarely need advertising.

moyo.title: Moyo
moyo.intro: A bright tomato-based sauce, often with crab or fish—sharp, generous, and inseparable from coastal tables.
moyo.tryIt: With crab, fish or on rice
moyo.heading: Heat,
moyo.headingEm: with a view of the water.
moyo.p1: Moyo is less a single recipe than a coastal attitude: tomato, fire, and whatever the lagoon or sea offered that morning.
moyo.p2: Eat it where the sauce is made to order. The difference between good and forgettable is measured in minutes.

igname-pilee.title: Igname pilée
igname-pilee.intro: Pounded yam—dense, elastic, and meant to be eaten with sauce, not as a side note.
igname-pilee.tryIt: With sauce arachide or palm sauce
igname-pilee.heading: The mortar still sets the pace.
igname-pilee.p1: Igname pilée is labour made edible. The sound of the pestle is part of the meal long before the plate arrives.
igname-pilee.p2: Respect the portion and the sauce. This is food that asks you to sit, not to scroll past it.

tale-tale.title: Talé-talé
tale-tale.intro: Sweet fried dough balls—golden, hot, and sold by the handful from pans that never seem to cool.
tale-tale.tryIt: Fresh from the oil, no ceremony
tale-tale.heading: Sugar,
tale-tale.p1: Talé-talé belongs to movement: bought between errands, shared without plates, finished before you reach the next corner.
tale-tale.p2: The best ones are the ones still too hot to hold comfortably.

sauce-arachide.title: Sauce arachide
sauce-arachide.intro: Peanut sauce—thick, savoury, and one of the country’s great shared languages at the table.
sauce-arachide.madeFrom: Groundnuts, oil, seasoning, often meat or fish
sauce-arachide.heading: Depth,
sauce-arachide.p1: Sauce arachide travels well across regions because it answers hunger with density: protein, fat, and the patience of slow cooking.
sauce-arachide.p2: Every household has a version. Ask whose, and you will learn more about the table than any menu can say.
